subject: Mutual Action Plan: deployment pathway & regional lock-in
messages:
From: Ashley Martin <ashley.martin@mediform.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: Contracts <contracts@mediform.com>, DevOps Team <devops@mediform.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Mutual action plan kickoff — deployment & region constraints

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team found Redwood's latency profile and cost controls compelling. We're ready to move into a formal MAP but need to be explicit about the deployment mode and region constraints up front. A couple of hard requirements from legal and our ops team:

- Production traffic must reside in the EU (Ireland) for the initial roll.
- We need a whitelistable vendor boundary and an option for dedicated capacity or on-prem if the audit flags data residency gaps.

Can you propose a short evaluation plan (2–4 week POC) that maps Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs, acceptance criteria, and an expected close timeline? Contracts will want to know the procurement steps as soon as possible.

I've attached our initial checklist and SOC ask.

Best,
Ashley Martin
Head of Integrations — Mediform

Attachments: MAP-Checklist.pdf (pdf), SOC2-Questions.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: Ashley Martin <ashley.martin@mediform.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan kickoff — deployment & region constraints

Hi Ashley — thanks for the clear ask.

Below is a concise MAP proposal we can commit to quickly; I put tentative owners and a recommended path based on the EU requirement and your whitelist request. Ill follow up with a calendar invite for a 30-minute alignment call.

High-level recommendation: begin with a Hosted EU-dedicated tenancy (Redwood Hosted with customer-dedicated capacity in eu-west-1) as the default POC. This gives you the fastest time-to-value while keeping the option to convert to Dedicated pools (reserved tenancy) or Private (VPC/on-prem) if the audit requires greater isolation.

MAP (2-3 week POC -> 4 week acceptance window -> procurement):
1) Week 0 (Alignment): sign MAP, shared success criteria, kick call (owners: jonas_weber, ashley.martin)
2) Week 1 (Sandbox + Integration): provide EU-hosted test endpoint, run basic traffic, attach SOC2 extracts for your security team (owner: karthik_iyer)
3) Week 2 (Scale & SLA Validation): run production-shaped traffic, measure p95 latency and token cost, validate autoscaling behavior (owner: lauren_bishop)
4) Week 3-4 (Acceptance & Close): acceptance testing, legal/contract negotiation, procurement paperwork; Option A: convert to Dedicated pools as committed capacity; Option B: run a Private deployment plan (timeline add-on)

Acceptance criteria (examples):
- p95 inference latency < 350ms for our standard 512-token prompt distribution
- Tail error rate < 0.5% over 24h
- Audit docs: SOC2 extracts + network topology + KMS integration checklist provided

Procurement path: HubSpot PO-> SOW -> DocuSign. If you need an expedited reserved-capacity quote, we can provide an estimate within 48 hours.

I've attached a working MAP spreadsheet (MAP-v2.xlsx) with milestone owners, acceptance checkboxes, and estimated costs for Hosted vs Dedicated.

Talk soon — proposed call: Wed 21 Jan 09:00 GMT (let me know if that works).

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
Phone: +1-415-555-0192

Attachments: MAP-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Jonas — thanks, that layout is super helpful. Quick clarifications from our side after an ops sync:

- Ireland region (eu-west-1) is required. Can the Hosted EU-dedicated tenancy guarantee single-region routing for the POC? We need a signed statement for the procurement file.
- If we hit a compliance blocker, we may ask for a Private deployment (VPC) timeline estimate. If you can include a ballpark delta in cost and time to move from Hosted->Dedicated->Private that would help.

Contracts asked: are there any standard SLAs for dedicated pools that differ materially from Hosted? Also, can you attach a recent SOC2 extract?

Confirming the call: Wed 21 Jan 09:00 GMT works for me.

—Ashley

Thanks for the alignment call yesterday — follow-ups from our side and the additional detail you requested.

1) Regional guarantee: for the Hosted EU-dedicated tenancy POC we can provide single-region routing to eu-west-1. We'll include an addendum statement in the SOW that commits POC traffic to eu-west-1 and documents fallback behavior (we will not route to other regions unless explicitly instructed or in the event of a catastrophic outage; fallback is defined in the runbook).

2) Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private delta (high level estimates):
- Hosted (EU-dedicated tenancy): Time to POC = 3 business days to stand up the tenant; Estimated monthly incremental cost = baseline API usage + managed tenancy premium (~+20%).
- Dedicated (reserved pool): Time to reserve and configure = 2–3 weeks; incremental cost for reserved baseline = commitment-dependent (typical uplift +40% for guaranteed capacity, lower per-token during heavy sustained usage).
- Private (VPC/on-prem): Time to delivery = 6–10 weeks (depends on network approvals & HSM/KMS integration); one-time setup fees apply + platform license.

3) SLA differences: Dedicated pools include a contractual latency and throughput target at commit levels; Hosted SLA for free tiers differs — for enterprise customers we can surface an SLA that matches Dedicated once a reserved capacity contract is executed. We'll attach the SLA excerpt to the SOW.

4) SOC2 extract: attached (SOC2-Audit-Extract.pdf). It contains the sections most procurement teams request: access control, encryption, and incident response summary.

Next steps (owners):
- Update MAP spreadsheet with the single-region statement and cost deltas (owner: karthik_iyer)
- Contracts to prepare SOW addendum and DocuSign room (owner: lauren_bishop)
- Mediform to confirm the procurement timeline and PO route (owner: Ashley)

Karthik
